neighbours.label: Specifying an amount for each member of a group rather than the aggregate amount for the whole group.
fire: The library has fourteen shelves, and each shelf holds thirty books.
Our workshop employs six assistants, each paid eighteen dollars for an hour of work.
The delivery contains eleven crates with a capacity of eight bottles each.
Each guest at the banquet receives three small pastries on a plate.
The farm has nine pens, with four goats housed in every pen.
A single ticket to the evening performance costs twenty-seven dollars.
The average backpack carried by a hiker weighs seven kilograms.
For the trip, every camper is allocated two liters of drinking water.
quiet: Across its fourteen shelves, the library can store four hundred twenty books altogether.
During one hour, our six workshop assistants earn one hundred eight dollars combined.
All eleven crates in the delivery can hold eighty-eight bottles in total.
The banquet kitchen prepared ninety small pastries for the entire group of guests.
Across the nine pens on the farm, the herd contains thirty-six goats altogether.
The entire group paid two hundred seventy dollars for tickets to the evening performance.
The hikers carried backpacks weighing seventy kilograms when all their loads were combined.
For the whole camp, the trip organizers allocated forty liters of drinking water.

notes: The card suggests a per-member versus aggregate distinction shared by the two poles. Exploration supported wage rates and mean versus combined weight, but some total statements also fired when they retained group counts. The registered near misses keep group counts in several cases to challenge this leakage rather than remove it.
